units.title: Linking words & cohesive devices
units.intro: Linking words (cohesive devices) join ideas: addition, contrast, cause and purpose. Each one has its own grammar. (This unit was Unit 8 before; Unit 8 now follows Textbook Unit 8.)

cards.title: Contrast and purpose
rule: so that + S + modal; in order to + Vbase.

examples.fix: Despite studying, he failed. / Although he studied, he failed.

examples.text: He revised so that he could pass.

cards.title: Connectors and the structures that follow them
body: **Contrast:** although / even though / though + clause; despite / in spite of + noun or -ing; however / nevertheless + new clause (after ; or .); whereas / while for direct comparison.
**Purpose:** to / in order to / so as to + base verb; so that + clause (often with can/could/would).
**Result:** so (after a comma); therefore / consequently / as a result (after ; or .); such + noun + that; so + adjective + that.
**Addition:** and; moreover / furthermore / in addition (after ; or .); not only ... but also.

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "Despite he studied, he failed."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** although/even though + S + V.
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "Despite he studied, he failed." breaks this rule.
**Step 3: Correct it.** "Despite studying, he failed. / Although he studied, he failed."

cards.answer: Despite studying, he failed. / Although he studied, he failed.

cards.title: Step by step: Linking words of contrast and purpose
body: **Step 1:** Although / even though / though + subject + verb: "Although it rained, we played."
**Step 2:** Despite / in spite of + noun or -ing: "Despite the rain, we played." / "In spite of being tired, she worked."
**Step 3:** However / nevertheless start a new sentence or follow a semicolon and take a comma: "It rained; however, we played."
**Step 4:** Whereas / while compare two contrasting facts: "Asmara is cool, whereas Massawa is hot."
**Step 5:** Purpose: to / in order to / so as to + verb; so that + subject + can/could/will/would + verb; "in order not to" for negative purpose.

**Example:** Join: "He was ill. He went to school." → "Although he was ill, he went to school." / "Despite being ill, he went to school." / "He was ill; however, he went to school." Purpose: "She saved money so that she could buy a bicycle."

cards.title: Mnemonic — "Although has a clause, Despite has a noun"
Exam tip
body: Never write "despite of" or "although…but". Use one contrast word per sentence.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: She bought the dress __________ it was expensive.
cards.why: The sentence shows a contrast (concession). 'Although' is followed by a full clause (subject + verb: 'it was expensive'). 'Despite' and 'In spite of' would require a noun phrase.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The team was at full strength despite the injury of one of its players.

options.A: The team wasn't complete because one of its players was injured.
options.B: The team was at full strength in spite of the injury of one of its players.
options.C: The team was at full strength because of the injury of one of its players.
options.D: The team wasn't at full strength although none of its players was injured.
options.E: The team was at full strength despite the injury of many of its players.

cards.why:
**Analysis:** The original sentence uses "despite" to show a contrast. 
**Step 1:** "In spite of" is the exact synonym for "despite".
**Step 2:** Choice B maintains the exact meaning: even though someone was injured, the team was still strong. 
**Step 3:** Choice A says it was not complete (wrong), Choice C says injury caused the strength (wrong).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: He ought to look forward to achieving his goal __________ the temporarily existing difficulties.
cards.why: The word **'despite'** is a preposition used to show contrast. It is followed by a noun phrase ('the temporarily existing difficulties'). 'Even though' would require a full clause.

cards.title: Conjunctive adverbs
rule: therefore / however / moreover join two clauses with a semicolon before and a comma after: *It rained; however, we played.*
Do not write Because… so… or Although… but… (double conjunction).

examples.text: Although she tried, but she failed.
The roads were blocked; however, buses ran.

cards.title: Punctuating conjunctive adverbs
body: Conjunctive adverbs (however, therefore, moreover, consequently, nevertheless, otherwise) are **not** conjunctions. They cannot join two clauses with only a comma.
Correct patterns: *It rained; **however**, we played.* or *It rained. **However**, we played.* or inside the clause: *We, **however**, played.*
Wrong: ✗ *It rained, however we played.* (comma splice).
Use only one connector per link: ✗ *Although it rained, but we played* → *Although it rained, we played.*

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "Although she tried, but she failed."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** therefore / however / moreover join two clauses with a semicolon before and a comma after: *It rained; however, we played.*
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "Although she tried, but she failed." breaks this rule.
**Step 3: Correct it.** "Although she tried, she failed."
**Check:** Do not write Because… so… or Although… but… (double conjunction).

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Pick the connector for the logic and for the structure that follows the blank.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Choose the clause which is connected correctly.

options.A: Because he'd never tried it before, he was very good at it.
options.B: Despite he'd never tried it before, he was very good at it.
options.C: In spite of he'd never tried it before, he was very good at it.
options.D: Since he'd never tried it before, he was very good at it.
options.E: Although he'd never tried it before, he was very good at it.

cards.why: The sentence shows a contrast (never tried it vs. very good at it). 'Although' is a conjunction followed by a full clause (subject + verb). 'Despite' and 'In spite of' must be followed by a noun or gerund, not a clause.

cards.title: Quick check

options.A: The exam was difficult; nevertheless, most students passed.
options.B: The exam was difficult, nevertheless most students passed.
options.C: The exam was difficult nevertheless, most students passed.
options.D: The exam was difficult; nevertheless most students, passed.

cards.why:
**Step 1:** "nevertheless" is a conjunctive adverb.

**Step 2:** It needs a semicolon (or full stop) before it and a comma after it.

**Step 3:** Only the first option follows this pattern.

**Tip:** Check both meaning (contrast, result, addition, purpose) and structure: although + clause; despite + noun/-ing; so that + clause; in order to + verb; ; however, + clause.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: "She practised every day; ____, she won the competition."
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Winning was a result of practising every day.

**Step 2:** "as a result" introduces a consequence.

**Step 3:** The others show contrast, example or condition.

**Tip:** Check both meaning (contrast, result, addition, purpose) and structure: although + clause; despite + noun/-ing; so that + clause; in order to + verb; ; however, + clause.

questions.label: 1. ________ the heavy storm and road blockages, the administrat

similar.q: ________ the heavy storm and road blockages, the a
The final chemistry revision class was canceled __

why: Answer B: Despite

The blank is followed by a noun phrase 'the heavy storm and road blockages' (no verb present) and introduces contrast. This requires a noun-governing concessive preposition: despite / in spite of + Noun Phrase.
Students often choose 'Although' (Option A) or 'Even though' (Option C) because they translate 'እኳ እንተ-... ምስ' similarly. Option D 'In spite' is incorrect because it lacks 'of'. Option B is correct.
questions.tip: Check both meaning (contrast, result, addition, purpose) and structure: although + clause; despite + noun/-ing; so that + clause; in order to + verb; ; however, + clause.

questions.q: The final chemistry revision class was canceled ________ the sudden illness of the professor.
questions.label: 2. The final chemistry revision class was canceled ________ the

similar.q: The final chemistry revision class was canceled __
Although the laboratory equipment was extremely ex

why: Answer B: because of
The blank is followed by a noun phrase 'the sudden illness of the professor', indicating a cause-and-effect relationship. This requires a prepositional cause marker: because of + Noun Phrase.

Students often choose 'because' (Option A) or 'since' (Option C) because they translate both as 'ስለ...'. However, 'because' requires a full clause (Subject + Verb), while 'because of' (Option B) is correct for noun phrases.
questions.tip: Check both meaning (contrast, result, addition, purpose) and structure: although + clause; despite + noun/-ing; so that + clause; in order to + verb; ; however, + clause.

questions.label: 3. Although the laboratory equipment was extremely expensive, _

similar.q: Although the laboratory equipment was extremely ex
She studied hard until midnight ________ she could

why: Answer D: [No connector]

'Although' is a subordinating conjunction at the beginning of the sentence to connect the clauses. In English, only one conjunction can connect two clauses; adding a second is a double-conjunction error.
Students often choose 'but' (Option A) because in Tigrinya, it is natural to pair concession with contrast (e.g., 'ድኻ እኳ እንተኾነ፡ ግን...'). Option D is correct because no extra connector is allowed.
questions.tip: Check both meaning (contrast, result, addition, purpose) and structure: although + clause; despite + noun/-ing; so that + clause; in order to + verb; ; however, + clause.

questions.q: She studied hard until midnight ________ she could pass the national biology examination.
questions.label: 4. She studied hard until midnight ________ she could pass the

similar.q: She studied hard until midnight ________ she could
________ being extremely tired after the long jour

why: Answer B: so that
The blank is followed by a full clause containing a modal verb ('she could pass...'). This requires a clause-based purpose connector: so that + Subject + modal + Verb.

Students often choose 'in order to' (Option A) or 'so as to' (Option C) because they translate both as 'ምእንቲ'. However, those infinitive-based connectors require a bare verb (in order to + V (base)), making Option B correct.
questions.tip: Check both meaning (contrast, result, addition, purpose) and structure: although + clause; despite + noun/-ing; so that + clause; in order to + verb; ; however, + clause.

He studied the grammar modules diligently; _______

why: Answer B: In spite of
The blank is followed by a gerund 'being' (no subject present) and introduces contrast. This requires a noun-governing concessive preposition: in spite of + Noun/V-ing.

Students often choose 'Although' (Option A) or 'Even though' (Option C) because they translate 'being tired' as a clause. Since there is no subject before 'being', the prepositional 'In spite of' (Option B) is correct.
questions.tip: Check both meaning (contrast, result, addition, purpose) and structure: although + clause; despite + noun/-ing; so that + clause; in order to + verb; ; however, + clause.

questions.label: 6. He studied the grammar modules diligently; ________, he achi

similar.q: He studied the grammar modules diligently; _______
________ the heavy storm and road blockages, the a

why: Answer A: consequently
The blank is preceded by a semicolon and followed by a comma, indicating a conjunctive adverb is required. The logical relationship is cause-and-effect (result).

Students often choose 'furthermore' (Option C) because it has the same punctuation. However, 'furthermore' indicates addition, while the logical context requires 'consequently' (Option A - as a result) to show the effect of his study.

questions.q: We will not be able to finish the project on time ________ everyone works much harder.
questions.label: 7. We will not be able to finish the project on time ________ e

similar.q: ________ the heavy storm and road blockages, the a

why: Answer B: unless
The sentence expresses a negative condition: we won't finish *unless* (if not) everyone works harder. This requires the negative conditional conjunction 'unless' (unless = if + not).

Students often choose 'if' (Option A) because they translate 'እንድሕር' directly. However, using 'if' would mean 'if everyone works harder, we won't finish', which is logically incorrect. Option B 'unless' is correct.
questions.tip: Check both meaning (contrast, result, addition, purpose) and structure: although + clause; despite + noun/-ing; so that + clause; in order to + verb; ; however, + clause.

similar.q: The final chemistry revision class was canceled __

why: Answer B: so as to
The blank is followed by a bare verb 'arrive', indicating a purpose relationship. This requires an infinitive-based purpose connector: so as to + V (base).
Students often choose 'so that' (Option A) because they translate it as 'ምእንቲ'. However, 'so that' requires a full clause (Subject + Verb), making 'so as to' (Option B) correct.

questions.q: The newly bought computer is very cheap; ________, its performance is excellent for research.
questions.label: 9. The newly bought computer is very cheap; ________, its perfo

similar.q: Although the laboratory equipment was extremely ex

why: Answer B: however
The blank is preceded by a semicolon and followed by a comma. The logical relationship is contrast: the computer is cheap (negative/neutral) but its performance is excellent (positive).

Students often choose 'moreover' (Option A) or 'therefore' (Option C) because they see the semicolon and comma. However, the contrastive context requires 'however' (Option B - yet/but) to show the opposing ideas.
questions.tip: Check both meaning (contrast, result, addition, purpose) and structure: although + clause; despite + noun/-ing; so that + clause; in order to + verb; ; however, + clause.

questions.q: Aster prefers studying physics, ________ her younger sister loves biology.
questions.label: 10. Aster prefers studying physics, ________ her younger sister

similar.q: She studied hard until midnight ________ she could

why: Answer A: whereas
The sentence compares two differing preferences directly (contrast), requiring a subordinating conjunction of contrast: Clause1 + whereas + Clause2.

Students often choose 'furthermore' (Option B) because they think it connects ideas, or 'despite' (Option C) which requires a noun phrase. Option A 'whereas' is correct because it directly contrasts two clauses.
questions.tip: Check both meaning (contrast, result, addition, purpose) and structure: although + clause; despite + noun/-ing; so that + clause; in order to + verb; ; however, + clause.

questions.q: ______ he was one of the most talented directors, he got only 5 percent of the vote.
why: Answer E: Despite the fact that
'Despite the fact that' is a correct complex conjunction for contrast. 'In spite' requires 'of' (In spite of the fact that). 'Despite' should NOT have 'of' immediately after it.

questions.q: True or false: "In spite of he was tired, he played" is correct.
questions.label: 20. True or false: "In spite of he was tired, he played" is correct.

similar.q: Correct: Despite it rained, we went.
Correct: In spite of she is young, she is wise.
similar.a: In spite of being young, she is wise.

why: False. "In spite of" is followed by a noun or -ing form, not a clause.
Correct forms: In spite of being tired / In spite of his tiredness / Although he was tired.
So the sentence is incorrect.
